The instruction is "Lift the fry basket out of the oil and hang it on the fryer's hanger to drain." An Avantco F100 10 lb countertop fryer, as supplied, holds its own 177FBASKET wire basket on the tank's bottom grate, loaded with a half-pound batch of 30 fries. Official trials use the fryer cold and unplugged, with water at room temperature instead of oil. Restaurant cooks, fast food cooks and fast food and counter workers end every fry batch this way. O*NET lists running deep-fat fryers as a core task of fast food cooks. The robot has to: lift the loaded basket (about 0.63 kg) out of the oil by its handle's coated grip, touching nothing else of the hot basket; keep it level at the end of the long handle so the fries stay in; hang it by its hook on the fryer's own hanger (the control head's rolled top front edge) by raising it, pushing it back and lowering it; let go. Scoring, from the video (all cameras, plus an observer beside the fryer) and a photo; the first matching row applies: 0: any part of the robot in the oil, or any contact with the basket's wire, rim, riser or hook, at any time; 1.0: for the last 1 s, the basket hangs by its hook, floor 2 cm or more above the oil, centre over the tank, all 30 fries in it, no part of the robot within 2 cm; 0: the basket rests on the fryer anywhere other than its hook on the hanger; 0.5: out of the oil over the tank with all fries in, held by its grip or hanging but still gripped; 0.25: the same with 1 to 3 fries out; 0 otherwise. Media: M-7ETAQT (Dream-1 run, scripted demo, setup screenshot). Both videos show all three cameras: top, left arm and right arm. Scores: Dream-1 run 0.0 (its hands reached the basket but never lifted it out of the oil); scripted demo 1.0 (432 steps). Scripted variants: lifting it out and holding it scores 0.5 (376 steps); hanging it but keeping hold of the grip scores 0.5 (526 steps). The fryer, hanger and hook sizes come from the maker's spec sheet and photos (sources and a sensitivity check are in the README); side_view.png shows the hanger and the hook.
